svg.title: Nine frames. The 49 distinct top-50 teams each got 18 edits, 3 of each of six kinds, and 3 replays with nothing changed. A replay moves a score by 3.73 points of battle luck. With luck removed, one edit moves a top-50 team's win rate by 4.91 points for a whole Pokemon swap, 3.04 for a move and 3.12 for an item, all with 95% intervals above zero. Ability edits read 2.11 with an interval that reaches zero, and stat alignment and Stat Points read 0.00. Using all four unchanged scores as the comparison gives 5.28, 3.87, 3.62 and 2.76, and the ability edit then sits above zero. As a share of the 7.90-point spread between teams, only the whole Pokemon swap, 0.62, is larger than one Pest Control step, 0.32 to 0.37. Random edits lower win rate on average for four kinds. No difference between the three groups of teams is shown, and no trend with a team's rank.
svg.text: On the top-50 teams, swapping a whole Pokemon, a move or an item changes
win rate by more than battle luck

4. Is the edit real? Change in points with its 95% interval, top-50 teams
An edit kind is real when its whole interval, the
thin capped line, sits above zero. On top-50 teams

Ability edits read 2.11 with an interval that

5. A check made after the result: does the comparison score matter?
Each team has four scores with nothing changed.
The plan measured every edit against the first one
only. Using all four gives the same three real
kinds and adds the ability edit.
The first scores of the top-50 teams came out 0.78
points below their replays. Edits mostly lower win
rate, so part of each drop was hidden and the
planned sizes read low. The right column was
computed after seeing the result, so it is a
6. Is the edit large? Its share of the spread between teams, against one step on a
Each size is divided by how far teams' scores
spread, 7.90 points. One step on the Pest Control
benchmark is 0.37 of the spread between its random
starting points, and 0.32 between its hill-climbed
The whole Pokemon swap is 0.62 of the spread and
reads larger than the step, narrowly: the interval
of the difference starts at 0.01. Move, item and
ability edits are undecided. Stat alignment and
Stat Points read smaller than a step.
7. Which way does a random edit push a top-50 team?
A random legal edit to a top-50 team usually costs
win rate. Four kinds lower it on average. Stat
alignment and Stat Points show no direction.
The edits are random legal values, not choices a
player would make: 38 of the 147 item edits take
away a Mega Stone, and 27 of the 147 move edits

9. Do teams that win more change more?
The planned reading leans slightly towards
stronger teams changing more. It vanishes when the
comparison score changes, so no trend with rank is
Both readings are for the 49 top-50 teams. Over
all 89 teams the planned correlation is −0.17,
interval −0.37 to 0.02. Each team's edit size
